canonicalExplanation.summary: A `<caption>` is a table's **name**. It goes right after `<table>`, is visible to everyone, and is announced when a screen-reader user reaches the table — so they know what it contains before diving into cells. Keep it short and specific; put longer explanations (units, data source, how to read it) in a note nearby. The `title` attribute is not a substitute: it's hidden from most users.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A support dashboard shows three tables in a row: response times, ticket volumes, satisfaction scores. A screen-reader user jumping between tables hears "table, 5 columns, 4 rows" three times — which is which? The caption Quarterly support response times distinguishes the table from two adjacent metrics tables. In this lesson you'll add a concise caption and a contextual note to a data table.

```predict
{"question": "Where must the caption element go?", "options": ["Anywhere inside the table", "As the first child of table"], "answer": 1, "why": "`<caption>` must be the first element inside `<table>`. CSS can still move it visually (caption-side)."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Heading hierarchy** and **Headers and scope** — captions name the whole table, headers name rows and columns.

sections.heading: The model: a short name plus a nearby note
sections.body:
```html
Quarterly support response times
QuarterMedian (hours)
Q14.2
Q23.1

Median time to first reply, business hours only. Source: helpdesk export, June 2026.

``` | Piece | Job | |---|---| | `caption`. | short, specific name, announced with the table. | | note (`aria-describedby`). | units, source, how to read. | | `title` attribute. | ✗ not reliably seen or announced. | ```reveal {"prompt": "Can a heading above the table replace the caption?", "answer": "A heading helps page navigation, but only caption is programmatically tied to the table. Use caption; add a heading too if the table starts a new section."} ```

sections.heading: Specific beats generic

includes: Add a concise, specific caption as the first child of table.
Provide context such as units and source in a linked note.

outcomes: Add a concise caption and contextual note to a data table.

examples.title: Telling three tables apart
examples.situation: The caption Quarterly support response times distinguishes the table from two adjacent metrics tables.
walkthrough: **Problem:** three adjacent metrics tables had no names, so screen readers announced only their size.
**Caption:** `<caption>Quarterly support response times</caption>` goes first in the response-time table; the others get "Monthly ticket volume" and "Customer satisfaction by channel".
**Note:** a paragraph linked with aria-describedby will read units and source: median hours, business hours only.
examples.result: Each table is announced by name, and learners know what the numbers mean.

examples.title: The title-only table
examples.situation: A pricing table has `title="Prices for 2026 plans"` and no caption.
walkthrough: Sighted mouse users see it only as a tooltip after hovering.
Keyboard and touch users never see it; many screen readers don't announce it consistently.
Fix: move the text into a `<caption>`.
examples.result: The table's name is visible and announced for everyone.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: The title attribute is the preferred accessible label for every table.
misconceptions.correction: title is hidden unless hovered and inconsistently announced. A caption, as the first child of table, is visible and programmatically associated; longer context belongs in a nearby note.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The title-only table", which users missed the table's name?

analogy.example: A caption is like the **label on a file folder**: you read it before opening the folder. A title attribute is like writing the label on the inside cover.
usefulFor: seeing notes as the folder's cover sheet
limitations: Folders don't get announced; tables do.
A caption should stay short, like a label, not a paragraph.

remediation.explanation: Imagine hearing only the caption, without seeing the table. Could you tell it apart from the tables around it? If not, make it more specific.

recap.summary: To add a concise caption and a contextual note, put a short, specific caption as the first child of table and place units, source and reading guidance in a nearby note linked with aria-describedby. Don't rely on the title attribute.
